filename: Opinion_ The importance and future development of perturbed parameter ensembles in climate and atmospheric science.pdf
title: Opinion: The importance and future development of perturbed parameter ensembles in climate and atmospheric science
testbed_rationale: This is a review/opinion article discussing the use and future of perturbed parameter ensembles (PPEs) in climate and atmospheric science; no original datasets were produced.
pain_points: Computational cost of running ensembles of complex high-resolution models
High dimensionality of parameter space and sparse sampling
Equifinality and error compensation obscuring physical causation and reliable projections
Representation errors and observational uncertainties when confronting models with observations
Over-fitting / over-tuning of models concealing structural deficiencies
Disentangling internal variability from parametric and structural uncertainty
Large data volumes produced by extensive ensembles
extraction_notes: The paper is an opinion/review paper resulting partly from the WCRP APPEAR workshop. The data availability section states: 'No original research data was generated in this article.' Mentions funding by U.S. NSF STC Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP).
